_meta: Five requests to a replicated service, each with the latency of the replica it landed on, used to show HEDGED REQUESTS: sending a second copy of a request to another replica after a short delay and taking whichever responds first, to cap tail latency caused by one slow replica. latencies_ms is each request's response time on its assigned replica -- four are fast (10-13ms) and one hit a slow replica (200ms), the classic tail. hedge_delay_ms is how long to wait before sending a duplicate (20ms): chosen above the typical latency (so fast requests finish before the hedge fires and no duplicate is sent) but below the tail (so slow requests trigger a hedge). fallback_ms is the latency of the second replica the hedge goes to (15ms, a healthy replica). Without hedging, each request waits for its own replica, so the slow one gives a 200ms tail. With hedging, a request still outstanding at hedge_delay_ms gets a duplicate sent to a fast replica, and its effective latency becomes min(original, hedge_delay + fallback) -- the slow request drops from 200ms to min(200, 20+15)=35ms, while the four fast requests (all under 20ms) finish before the hedge and are unchanged, so only one extra request is sent. latencies_ms, hedge_delay_ms, and fallback_ms are the fixture; every effective latency, the tail, and the extra-request count are computed.
